arguments.topic: automated brain extraction skull stripping MRI deep learning

rows.title: Automated neonatal nnU-Net brain MRI extractor trained on a large multi-institutional dataset.
rows.modality: Neonatal brain MRI, including high- and low-resolution and motion-degraded images
rows.dataset: HEAL study (433 training participants); NIH and dHCP evaluation datasets
rows.summary: ANUBEX enables automatic neonatal brain extraction across acquisition settings and achieves higher aggregate Dice scores than five publicly available methods.

rows.title: Brain extraction on MRI scans in presence of diffuse glioma: Multi-institutional performance evaluation of deep learning methods and robust modality-agnostic training.
rows.method: Deep learning architectures with modality-agnostic training
rows.modality: Multiparametric brain MRI with brain tumors
rows.dataset: Private institutional cohorts and TCIA collections (3,340 scans)
rows.summary: Evaluates deep learning brain extraction across institutions and introduces modality-agnostic training to support available MRI modalities without retraining.

rows.title: Towards fully automated deep-learning-based brain tumor segmentation: is brain extraction still necessary?
rows.method: Deep learning tumor segmentation pipeline trained and tested without skull stripping
rows.metric_values: Brain extraction method choice can compromise tumor segmentation performance by up to 15.7%
rows.summary: Shows that omitting brain extraction can provide competitive tumor segmentation performance while reducing processing time and avoiding skull-stripping errors.

rows.title: A general skull stripping of multiparametric brain MRIs using 3D convolutional neural network.
rows.method: EnNet: ensemble neural network based on 3D convolutional neural networks
rows.modality: Multiparametric brain MRI, including healthy and pre-/post-operative GBM scans
rows.dataset: UPMC and TCIA retrospective dataset (815 cases with/without GBM)
rows.summary: Introduces automatic multicenter brain extraction for healthy and GBM scans and evaluates 15 MRI modality combinations, finding the best performance with all modalities.

rows.title: An End-To-End Pipeline for Fully Automatic Morphological Quantification of Mouse Brain Structures From MRI Imagery.
rows.method: DeepBrainIPP: deep learning skull stripping with data augmentation, atlas registration, and a dedicated small-structure segmentation model
rows.modality: In vivo and ex vivo mouse brain T2-weighted MRI
rows.dataset: private cohort (172 in-house images augmented to 4,040 samples)
rows.metric_values: Skull stripping: average Dice 0.96, residual volume 2.18%; atlas registration: average cross-correlation 0.98; small-structure segmentation: average Dice 0.89, residual volume error 5.32%
rows.summary: Provides an automated mouse brain processing pipeline combining skull stripping and atlas registration with direct segmentation of small structures through a web interface.

rows.title: k-strip: A novel segmentation algorithm in k-space for the application of skull stripping
rows.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
rows.method: k-strip: deep learning skull stripping directly in complex-valued k-space
rows.dataset: not stated (four datasets from different institutions, approximately 200,000 MRI slices)
rows.metric_values: Dice 92%–99%; Hausdorff distance <5.5 pixels; Dice up to 99% above the eye region
rows.summary: Demonstrates skull stripping directly in MRI k-space while preserving phase information and enabling anonymization before image reconstruction.

rows.title: Automated pediatric brain tumor imaging assessment tool from CBTN: Enhancing suprasellar region inclusion and managing limited data with deep learning.
rows.method: Separate nnU-Net-based models for skull stripping, whole-tumor segmentation, and enhancing-tumor segmentation
rows.modality: Pediatric brain MRI with single T2/FLAIR or multiple T1-Gd and T2/FLAIR sequences
rows.dataset: not stated (multi-institutional cohort of 527 pediatric patients; 336 for skull stripping and 489 for tumor segmentation)
rows.metric_values: Skull-stripping Dice 0.98 ± 0.01 (median 0.98) for both single- and multi-parametric models; single-/multi-parametric Dice correlation r >0.80 (P <.05); whole-tumor Dice: T2 0.84 ± 0.17 (median 0.90), FLAIR 0.82 ± 0.19 (median 0.89); enhancing-tumor Dice: T1-Gd+FLAIR 0.65 ± 0.35 (median 0.79), T1-Gd+T2 0.64 ± 0.36 (median 0.79)
rows.summary: Develops pediatric skull-stripping models that include sellar/suprasellar regions and tumor segmentation models accommodating limited data and missing MRI sequences.

rows.title: RU-Net: skull stripping in rat brain MR images after ischemic stroke with rat U-Net.
rows.method: RU-Net: U-shaped deep network integrating residual connections, batch normalization, and pooling-index transmission
rows.modality: Rat brain diffusion-weighted imaging and T2-weighted MRI after ischemic stroke
rows.dataset: private cohort (two in-house datasets, each containing 55 subjects)
rows.summary: Introduces an end-to-end skull-stripping network for rat brain MRI after stroke that outperforms several existing methods on two imaging modalities.

rows.title: SynthStrip: skull-stripping for any brain image.
rows.method: SynthStrip: learning-based brain extraction trained on synthetic images generated from anatomical segmentations
rows.modality: Brain MRI across acquisition protocols, contrasts, resolutions, and age groups
rows.dataset: not stated (entirely synthetic training dataset; diverse acquired images for evaluation)
rows.summary: Uses broadly varied synthetic training images to enable a single skull-stripping model to generalize across real brain imaging protocols without target-contrast training data.

rows.title: ASMCNN: An efficient brain extraction using active shape model and convolutional neural networks
rows.method: ASMCNN: modified active shape model and CNN with CRF, Gaussian-process, and rule-based post-processing
rows.modality: Brain MRI processed as 2D sagittal image sequences
rows.summary: Combines grouped shape priors with CNN-based contour refinement to improve brain extraction across variable MRI appearances.
